title: Uniform atlas for symbols modulo one lower operator order
statement: Use $\mathbf R,\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field] and the symbol, operator and distribution conventions of [def-sfb-symbol-pseudodifferential-operators]. Let $N$ be a compact oriented smooth manifold without boundary of dimension $m\geq1$, with smooth Riemannian metric and positive volume form $dV$, and let $E,F$ be smooth finite-rank real vector bundles. There exist finitely many coordinate charts $U_i$ trivializing $E,F$, real $\chi_i,\psi_i\in C_c^\infty(U_i)$ with $\sum_i\chi_i=1$ and $\psi_i=1$ on a neighborhood of $\operatorname{supp}\chi_i$, and compact sets $K_i\Subset U_i$ in chart coordinates, with the following property simultaneously for every integer $s$. For every $A\in\Psi^s(E,F)$ there are smooth matrix symbols $a_i\in S^s$ on $\mathbf R^m\times\mathbf R^m$, each supported in $K_i$ in the $x$ variable and satisfying global uniform symbol estimates, such that $$A-\sum_i\chi_i\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Op}(a_i)\psi_i\in\Psi^{s-1}(E,F).$$ The charts, cutoffs and compact sets are independent of both $A$ and $s$. The remainder membership is for the given operators on all distributions. The statement allows arbitrary symbols of type $S^s_{1,0}$; it does not require homogeneous leading symbols.

source.place: WANTED locally. Supplemental Demailly, Differential and pseudodifferential operators on manifolds, section 3, read online at https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/analytic_geometry_2019/pseudodiff.pdf; 3.5–3.6, p.7, fixed partition quantization and lower-order discrepancies; supporting coordinate-change/localization statement formulated by the agent for general symbols (not only homogeneous symbols).

proof.text: Choose a finite cover by coordinate domains $U_i$ trivializing both bundles: intersect local trivializations and shrink coordinate balls, then use compactness. The subordinate-partition theorem with $S=N$ gives smooth real $\chi_i$ with $\sum_i\chi_i=1$ and closed supports contained in $U_i$. They are compact since $N$ is compact Hausdorff. The separating-cutoff theorem applied to the disjoint closed sets $N\setminus U_i$ and $\operatorname{supp}\chi_i$ gives a real $\psi_i$ vanishing near the former and equal to one near the latter. Its support is a compact subset of $U_i$. Set $K_i$ equal to its support in chart coordinates. These choices involve only $N,E,F$. The hypotheses for the two cited theorems hold: $N$ is Hausdorff, sigma-compact (already compact), and normal (disjoint closed subsets are compact, and finitely many separating Hausdorff neighborhoods separate them).

source.place: WANTED locally; Demailly, Differential and pseudodifferential operators on manifolds, section 3, (3.3)--(3.6), printed pp.6--7, and (3.12)--(3.14), pp.9--10, read online at https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/analytic_geometry_2019/pseudodiff.pdf. Agent-written localization details using the cited DAG interfaces; the notes do not prove this full arbitrary-symbol, all-distributions formulation.

proof.text: Fix any integer $s$ and any $A\in\Psi^s(E,F)$. By the definition write $A=\sum_j\alpha_j\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Op}(b_j)\beta_j+R$ in finitely many charts $V_j$, with $b_j\in S^s$ and compact spatial cutoffs. Amplitude reduction applied to $\alpha_j(x)b_j(x,\xi)\beta_j(y)$ gives smooth kernels off the diagonal, and equality for the transposed actions on all distributions. Consequently $\chi_i A(1-\psi_i)$ is smoothing: its local amplitudes have the extra factor $\chi_i(x)(1-\psi_i(y))$, which vanishes near the diagonal since $\psi_i=1$ near $\operatorname{supp}\chi_i$. All spatial supports remain compact inside $V_j\times V_j$, so these smooth kernels extend by zero. In the convention using $dV(y)=v_j(y)\,dy$ their kernels are divided by the smooth positive $v_j(y)$; this preserves smoothness. The localized original $R$ is smooth as well. Thus $A-\sum_i\chi_i A\psi_i$ is smoothing, with the equality obtained from $\sum_i\chi_i=1$ on distributions.

source.place: WANTED locally; Demailly, Differential and pseudodifferential operators on manifolds, section 3, (3.3)--(3.6), printed pp.6--7, and (3.12)--(3.14), pp.9--10, read online at https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/analytic_geometry_2019/pseudodiff.pdf. Agent-written localization details using the cited DAG interfaces; the notes do not prove this full arbitrary-symbol, all-distributions formulation.

proof.text: For each $i,j$, put $\gamma_{ij}=\psi_i\alpha_j$. Its support is compact in $U_i\cap V_j$: it lies in the intersection of the two compact supports, each contained in its chart. Omit zero terms. Smooth separation supplies $\zeta_{ij}$ compactly supported in $U_i\cap V_j$ and equal to one near $\operatorname{supp}\gamma_{ij}$. Decompose $\psi_i\alpha_j\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Op}(b_j)\beta_j$ into $L_{ij}=\gamma_{ij}\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Op}(b_j)(\beta_j\zeta_{ij}\,\cdot)$ and the term with $1-\zeta_{ij}$. The latter has compact amplitude vanishing near the diagonal and hence is smoothing by amplitude reduction, exactly as in step 2. Therefore $\psi_i A=\sum_j L_{ij}+R_i$ for a smooth global kernel $R_i$. Both spatial variables of $L_{ij}$ are now localized in the overlap; this is why changing coordinates there is legitimate.

source.place: WANTED locally; Demailly, Differential and pseudodifferential operators on manifolds, section 3, (3.3)--(3.6), printed pp.6--7, and (3.12)--(3.14), pp.9--10, read online at https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/analytic_geometry_2019/pseudodiff.pdf. Agent-written localization details using the cited DAG interfaces; the notes do not prove this full arbitrary-symbol, all-distributions formulation.

proof.text: Apply coordinate change to $L_{ij}$ from the $V_j$ coordinates and frames to those of $U_i$, restricting both coordinate domains to their overlap. The coordinate transition is a diffeomorphism and the two frame transitions are smooth invertible real matrices, so all hypotheses hold with order $s$, output cutoff $\gamma_{ij}$ and input cutoff $\beta_j\zeta_{ij}$. Obtain $L_{ij}=\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Op}(q_{ij})\mu_{ij}+R_{ij}$ on all distributions. Here $q_{ij}\in S^s$ has compact $x$ support in the overlap, $R_{ij}$ is smooth, and $\mu_{ij}=1$ near $\operatorname{supp}\gamma_{ij}\cup\operatorname{supp}(\beta_j\zeta_{ij})$. Write $e_{ij}$ for the leading expression supplied by that theorem: the cotangent and frame transform of $b_j$, multiplied by $\gamma_{ij}\beta_j\zeta_{ij}$ and averaged under $a(x,\xi)\mapsto\overline{a(x,-\xi)}$. Thus $q_{ij}-e_{ij}\in S^{s-1}$ and $(\mu_{ij}-1)e_{ij}=0$. Symbols, cutoffs and smooth kernels extend by zero into the fixed chart as asserted by the theorem. Density-dual transport includes its absolute Jacobian; no volume-preserving coordinate change is assumed.

source.place: WANTED locally; Demailly, Differential and pseudodifferential operators on manifolds, section 3, (3.3)--(3.6), printed pp.6--7, and (3.12)--(3.14), pp.9--10, read online at https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/analytic_geometry_2019/pseudodiff.pdf. proof.text: For each $i,j$ consider $D_{ij}=\chi_i\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Op}(q_{ij})(\mu_{ij}-1)\psi_i$ in the fixed chart. Its compactly supported amplitude is $c_{ij}(x,y,\xi)=\chi_i(x)q_{ij}(x,\xi)(\mu_{ij}(y)-1)\psi_i(y)$. Its diagonal value has order $s-1$, because it equals $\chi_i(x)(q_{ij}-e_{ij})(x,\xi)(\mu_{ij}(x)-1)\psi_i(x)$ by step 4. Multiplication by these fixed spatial functions preserves the derivative bounds by the finite Leibniz sum. Amplitude reduction gives $D_{ij}=\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Op}(t_{ij})\nu_{ij}+S_{ij}$, where $t_{ij}-c_{ij}(x,x,\xi)\in S^{s-1}$. Therefore $t_{ij}\in S^{s-1}$ and $S_{ij}$ is smooth. Choose an output cutoff equal to one on the compact $x$ support of $t_{ij}$ using smooth separation. This is a defining finite representation in $\Psi^{s-1}(E,F)$. The real-part and transpose clauses in amplitude reduction ensure this is the same $D_{ij}$ on every distribution.

source.place: WANTED locally; Demailly, Differential and pseudodifferential operators on manifolds, section 3, (3.3)--(3.6), printed pp.6--7, and (3.12)--(3.14), pp.9--10, read online at https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/analytic_geometry_2019/pseudodiff.pdf. Agent-written localization details using the cited DAG interfaces; the notes do not prove this full arbitrary-symbol, all-distributions formulation.

proof.text: Set $a_i(x,\xi)=\psi_i(x)\sum_jq_{ij}(x,\xi)$, extended by zero to $\mathbf R^m$. Each $q_{ij}$ has compact support inside the overlap and a smooth zero extension. Its local symbol estimates on a compact neighborhood of that support give global estimates after extension. Finite sums and the Leibniz rule therefore give global uniform estimates for $a_i\in S^s$, with $x$ support contained in the fixed $K_i$. Since $\chi_i\psi_i=\chi_i$, steps 3--5 give $\chi_i A\psi_i-\chi_i\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Op}(a_i)\psi_i\in\Psi^{s-1}$. Combine these finitely many differences with the smoothing remainder of step 2. Smooth kernels belong to every order by the empty-sum clause; finite sums of order $s-1$ representations are obtained by concatenating their chart terms and adding their kernels. This proves the required remainder membership on all distributions. Only the symbols and the intermediate overlap cutoffs depend on $A,s$; the output charts, $\chi_i,\psi_i,K_i$ were fixed in step 1. No homogeneity was used.
